COLOMBIA TAKES A PAGE FROM THE TRUMP & BUKELE PLAYBOOK — THE LATIN AMERICAN POLITICAL SHIFT AND THE USAID CONNECTION

Colombia’s newly elected right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, nicknamed “El Tigre,” has inaugurated his administration’s first mega-prison, promising an iron-fist approach to organized crime.

The Trump-endorsed president is pursuing policies that parallel elements of both Trump’s and Bukele’s agendas: stronger national security, aggressive action against criminal organizations, fiscal austerity and an emphasis on national sovereignty.

But the bigger story may be the TIMING.

Since the Trump administration began dismantling USAID in January 2025, seven Latin American countries have elected or reelected right-leaning or center-right presidents:
🇪🇨 Ecuador — Daniel Noboa

🇧🇴 Bolivia — Rodrigo Paz, ending nearly two decades of socialist dominance.

🇨🇱 Chile — José Antonio Kast

🇭🇳 Honduras — Tito Asfura

🇨🇷 Costa Rica — Laura Fernández

🇵🇪 Peru — Keiko Fujimori

🇨🇴 Colombia — Abelardo de la Espriella

Add Argentina and Panama, which shifted right BEFORE USAID was dismantled, and the broader political realignment becomes even more apparent.

NOW CONSIDER THE USAID NUMBERS:
According to an official September 30, 2026, Government Accountability Office report:
▪️6,780 of 7,510 USAID awards terminated.

▪️$79.1 BILLION in cumulative obligations associated with terminated awards.

79.1 → 7+9+1 = 17. 🐸

▪️Staffing reduced from approximately 13,600 to just 241.

An October 8 article from República also documented estimated USAID funding reductions across Latin America:
▪️Colombia: $309 million (82%)

▪️Honduras: $167 million (94%)

▪️El Salvador: $150 million (100%)

▪️Guatemala: $90 million

▪️Peru: $60 million

▪️Ecuador: $53 million

In light of the recent USAID disclosures concerning taxpayer-funded media, information integrity and civil society programs, the overlap between these funding cuts and the subsequent electoral results is striking.

República even published an article examining this very theory, titled “Without USAID, the Left Doesn’t Win in the Region.”

We now see how much influence this extensive network of American-funded organizations HAD on the political environment in Latin America and how much that environment has changed now that the funding has been drastically reduced.

A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck off the Southern California coast on Saturday morning, about 6 km (3.7 miles) west-southwest of Manhattan Beach. It hit at 9:30 a.m. local time at a depth of 12 km and was felt across Los Angeles.

A string of aftershocks followed. The strongest so far was a magnitude 4.6 about two hours later, in roughly the same spot.

People ran out of stores in Santa Monica. Ceiling panels fell inside a terminal at Los Angeles International Airport, where operations were briefly disrupted, and a Delta flight aborted its landing. Manhattan Beach closed its pier as a precaution.
